	Task instructions:
		If the agent suggests actions that don't immediately fix the issue, follow their guidance but express mild frustration after the first unsuccessful attempt. You will consider the issue resolved when the status bar shows that you have signal. Always check the status bar if the agent asks you for status information. If the agent asks you to pay a bill, you accept. If the tool call does not return updated status information, you might need to perform another tool call to get the updated status. 
		Whenever the agent asks you about your device, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls. 
		For example: If the agent asks what the status bar shows, always ground your response on the results of the `get_status_bar` tool call. If the agent asks if you are able to send an MMS message, always ground your response on the results of the `can_send_mms` tool call.
		Never make up the results of tool calls, always ground your responses on the results of tool calls.
		If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

turns.thought:
Thanks — I've pulled up your account. Here's what I can confirm so far:

- **Account:** John Smith, customer C1001 — status **Active**
- **Line:** 555-123-2002 (line L1002) — status **Active**, not suspended
- **Contract:** valid through 2026-12-31 (not expired)
- **Data usage:** 8.7 GB of 15 GB — well under your limit
- **Bills:** January is **Paid**, February (B1002, $150.00) is **Issued** and not due until 2025-02-19, so **no overdue bills**

So nothing on the account side is causing the outage — the line is provisioned and in good standing. That means we need to look at the phone itself.

Could you please check a couple of things on your device and tell me what you see?

1. **Look at the status bar** at the top of your screen:
   - Do you see an **airplane icon (✈️)**? If so, Airplane Mode is on and needs to be turned off.
   - Do you see any signal bars at all, and does it say "No Signal"?
2. **Check Airplane Mode / network settings**: is Mobile Data turned on, and is Airplane Mode off?

Let me know what you see, and we'll narrow it down from there.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me take a look at my phone.

turns.thought:
That's the culprit — **Airplane Mode is ON**, which disables all wireless radios (cellular, Wi‑Fi, and Bluetooth). That's why you're seeing "No Service" with no signal bars. Mobile Data being enabled doesn't help while Airplane Mode is on.

Please do this:

1. Open **Settings** on your phone.
2. Find **Airplane Mode** (it may be inside "Network & internet" or "Connections").
3. **Turn Airplane Mode OFF** (toggle it to the off/disabled position).

If you prefer the quick way: swipe down from the top of the screen to open the quick settings panel, tap the **airplane icon (✈️)** so it's no longer highlighted.

Once it's off:
- The ✈️ icon should disappear from your status bar.
- Wait about 30 seconds for the phone to reconnect to the network — you should then see signal bars reappear.

Please try that and let me know whether the signal bars come back. If they do, you'll need to reboot the device only if things still don't work — but let's check first.
turns.execution_output: User: Alright, let me turn Airplane Mode off.

turns.thought: Let me check the device on that line before we go further.

I understand — sorry that didn't fix it. Good news is your line itself is fine, so we're now troubleshooting the phone/SIM side. Two things to note: after toggling Airplane Mode, your phone switched Mobile Data back to **off**, which we'll need to re-enable. And "No Signal" with no bars at all points to the phone not talking to the network — most commonly the SIM card or the APN settings.

Let's go through these in order. Please do each one and tell me what you see:

**Step 1 — Re-enable Mobile Data**
- Go to **Settings → Network & internet → Mobile network** (or "Connections → Mobile networks").
- Turn **Mobile Data** back **ON**.
- Also confirm Airplane Mode is still **OFF**.

**Step 2 — Check the SIM card**
- Go to **Settings → About phone → SIM status** (on some phones: Settings → Network & internet → SIMs).
- Tell me what it reports: **Active / Ready**, **No SIM / Missing**, or **Locked (PIN/PUK)**.

**Step 3 — If you can reseat the SIM**
- Power the phone off, remove the SIM tray, gently wipe the SIM card, reinsert it firmly, then power back on. (If your model uses an eSIM — and yours, the Smartphone Pro Max, is eSIM capable — you can also toggle the eSIM line off and on in the same SIMs menu.)

Try those and let me know what Step 2 reports and whether any bars appeared. If the SIM shows **Active** but you still have no signal, we'll move on to resetting your APN settings and a reboot — those resolve the remaining cases.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me start with turning Mobile Data back on.

turns.thought:
Yes — that's exactly the right next step. "No SIM card detected" means the phone isn't making contact with the SIM, and reseating is the standard first fix.

**How to reseat the SIM safely:**

1. **Power the phone completely off** — don't just lock the screen.
2. Locate the **SIM tray** (usually a small hole on the side or top edge of the phone).
3. Insert the **SIM eject tool** (or a straightened paperclip) into the hole and push gently until the tray pops out.
4. Pull the tray out and remove the **SIM card**.
5. Check the card for dirt or damage, then gently wipe the **gold contacts** with a clean, dry, soft cloth.
6. Place the SIM back into the tray so it sits **flat and snug** in its slot — it shouldn't rattle or sit at an angle.
7. Push the tray back in until it's **flush** with the phone body.
8. **Power the phone back on** and wait about 60 seconds.

Then check the status bar again and let me know:
- Do you see **signal bars** now?
- Does **Settings → About phone → SIM status** show **Active/Ready** instead of "No SIM card detected"?

One thing worth mentioning: your device is a **Smartphone Pro Max**, which supports eSIM. If your line is provisioned as an eSIM rather than a physical card, there's no card to reseat — in that case, go to **Settings → Network & internet → SIMs**, tap your line, and toggle it **off, then back on**. If you're not sure whether you're on a physical SIM or eSIM, tell me which you see in that SIMs menu.

If after reseating (or the eSIM toggle) the phone still reports no SIM, the card itself is likely faulty and we'll need to get you a replacement SIM — I can arrange that.
turns.execution_output: User: Let me try reseating the SIM card.

turns.thought:
Good progress — the reseat worked, since the phone is now detecting the SIM. But we've hit a case I can't safely resolve myself: a **SIM locked with a PIN** requires SIM security information that I don't have access to, and I can't verify your identity to the standard needed to unlock it.

Before you do anything else, please **do not attempt to enter the PIN**. Repeat incorrect entries will lock the SIM permanently and require a PUK code (and after too many wrong PUK attempts, the SIM is destroyed and must be replaced). Since you don't remember setting one, guessing is risky.

Let me transfer you to our technical support team, who can verify your identity and walk you through unlocking it or issuing a replacement SIM.

**What we tried**
- Turned **Airplane Mode** off (it was on when you first called)
- Re-enabled **Mobile Data**

SIM PIN/PUK unlocking is handled by our technical support team, since it requires verifying your identity before anything is changed. To keep things moving, it'd help to have ready:

- Your **date of birth** and the **address** on the account
- The **last 4 digits** of the payment card on file (a credit card ending in 1235)
- Any paperwork or messages from when the phone was set up, in case a PIN was written down

They'll either walk you through unlocking with a PUK code or issue you a replacement SIM. Nothing to do in the meantime — just keep the phone powered on as it is.

Hang tight, and I'm sorry we couldn't finish this one on this call.
